speaker: Doctor
text: That is very concerning; have you noticed if these red bumps are itchy, painful, or filled with fluid? Also, have you recently traveled to an area with a high prevalence of mosquito-borne diseases like malaria or dengue?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (infestation by Sarcoptes scabiei).

I suspect this is due to the intense pruritus and the specific location of the rash, especially since you have diabetes which can alter skin reactions. Have anyone else in your household or close contacts been experiencing similar itching or bumps recently?
